question: Should OpenClaw publish a supported OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and if so which surfaces should it cover?
rationale: The implementation would define a public API, auth, versioning, and client-generation contract across stable Gateway surfaces, so automation should not choose the boundary without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Keep Open For API Direction
options.body: Use this issue to decide the supported schema scope and security/versioning contract before adding any generated artifact or runtime route.

options.title: Scope To HTTP-Only Spec
options.body: Sponsor a narrow implementation for selected Gateway HTTP endpoints with auth warnings, generated-schema drift checks, and docs.

options.title: Fold Into SDK Track
options.body: Redirect the request to the public SDK/schema-package track if maintainers decide OpenAPI is not the supported custom-client surface.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For API Direction
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the supported schema scope and security/versioning contract before adding any generated artifact or runtime route.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent Gateway protocol work is closest to the public API/schema contract boundary this decision would define.
